paragraphs.text: Claude Code: From Coding to Workflow Design

Internal Computational Team
January 2026
We're stuck in an old mental model of development.
Old: Developer writes code line by line
New: Developer describes outcomes
Old: IDE assists with autocomplete
New: Agent plans and executes
Old: Human is the executor
New: Human supervises and validates
Engineers now design systems, not write software.
One person built a Polymarket tool in 2 hours without writing code
The technique mattered more than which AI was used
Architecture and process design become primary skills
"The outcome is defined by the process, not the model." — Mike.tech
Communicate intent structurally—let agents find the implementation.
Use XML tags: <task>, <context>, <constraints>, <output_format>
Code-Level: "Write a function that..." → Focus on implementation
Abstract: "I need to transform X into Y" → Focus on intent
"It's like I was driving a race car in first gear the whole time."
Every CLAUDE.md update compounds your efficiency gains.
Session 1: Write CLAUDE.md with basic project context
Session 5: Add common commands, conventions, warnings
Session 20: Refined skills, custom hooks, team patterns
Session 100: Agent works like a trained team member
Claude Code is a general agent, not just a coding tool.
February 2025: Launch as CLI research preview
October 2025: Web launch on claude.ai
November 2025: $1B revenue run-rate
January 2026: Multi-agent infrastructure (v2.1.0)
Claude Code automates anything you can type into a computer.
File system access (read, write, edit)
Command execution (shell access)
Context awareness (understands project structure)
Autonomous operation (minimal supervision)
"Agents are tools in a loop" — Simon Willison
Claude Code is an LLM with permission to access a file system.
Web Chatbot: Stateless conversations, copy-paste snippets
Claude Code: Persistent filesystem access, direct file read/write
Web Chatbot: Describe your environment, human executes commands
Claude Code: Agent explores and executes autonomously
Claude Code's power comes from its simplicity.
No heavyweight protocols needed
Skills are just markdown files the agent reads
Four tools (read, write, edit, bash) outperform complex ecosystems
Outsources hard parts to the LLM harness and computer environment
Transformers have a hard context limit due to O(N²) complexity.
Attention mechanism scales quadratically with sequence length
Context window is a hard limit on what the model can "see"
Everything the model knows about your task must fit in this window
Wasted tokens = reduced capability
Context engineering is the fundamental skill for agent work.
Minimal system prompts: <1,000 tokens vs competitors' 10,000+
File-based planning: External markdown preserves info across sessions
Progressive disclosure: Load tool docs only when needed
Pre-session artifacts: Research sessions → implementation sessions
The /status command lets you monitor context usage in real-time.
Current session: percentage of context window used
Session reset: when the 5-hour window resets
Weekly usage across Opus and Sonnet models
Demo the /status command
Subagents spawn fresh context windows for parallel tasks.
Each subagent gets its own fresh context window
Example: 36 files ÷ 3 subagents = 12 files each
Prevents main agent from sequential overload
Enables parallel processing
A taxonomy of agentic patterns has emerged from practice.
Context & Memory: Context-minimization, dynamic injection
Feedback Loops: Self-critique, reflection, spec-as-test
Orchestration: Plan-then-execute, phase separation
Tool Use: CLI-first, code-over-API
Skills are markdown files that Claude loads on demand.
Just markdown files with YAML metadata
Brief summaries scanned before full load
Shareable across models and tools
No heavyweight protocols
140+ scientific skills cover databases, packages, and integrations.
28+ Scientific databases (OpenAlex, PubMed, ChEMBL, UniProt)
55+ Python packages (RDKit, Scanpy, PyTorch)
15+ Scientific integrations (Benchling, DNAnexus)
Categories: Bioinformatics, Cheminformatics, Clinical Research, ML/AI
MCP servers can waste 7-9% of context window on unused tools.
Anti-MCP: Tools you never use still consume tokens
Alternative: CLI tools with README loaded on-demand
Pro-MCP: Convenience of always-available tools
Trade-off: Convenience vs. context efficiency
Git worktree enables running multiple Claude sessions in parallel.
git worktree add ../feature-auth feature/auth
git worktree add ../feature-api feature/api
Run Claude Code in each (separate terminals)
Boris Cherny (Claude Code creator) runs 5 Claudes in parallel!
Workflow, context, and parallelization are the efficiency pillars.
1. Workflow Design: Define what agents should do
2. Context Engineering: Optimize what agents can see
3. Parallelization: Scale by running multiple agents
Once you trust the workflow, multiplying it becomes obvious
Getting started requires one npm install and authentication.
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
claude --version
cd your-project && claude
First run: authenticate, create ~/.claude/, optionally run /init
Subscription plans range from $20 to $200/month.
Pro: $20/month — Light usage, small repos
Max 5x: $100/month — Moderate usage, larger repos
Max 20x: $200/month — Heavy usage, complex projects
Usage shared across Claude web, desktop, and Code
A customizable statusline displays model, cost, and tokens.
model.display_name: Current model
tokens.input / tokens.output: Token counts
cost.current / cost.total: Cost tracking
Setup: /statusline show the model name and context usage percentage
The /status command shows session info, config, and usage.
Status: Version, session ID, model, MCP servers, memory
Config: Preferences, theme, checkpoints
Usage: Context percentage, weekly limits
Demo switching between tabs with Tab key
CLAUDE.md gives Claude persistent project-specific context.
# Project Name, ## Tech Stack, ## Commands, ## Conventions
Example: Python 3.11, FastAPI, PostgreSQL
Example: pytest tests/, uvicorn main:app --reload
Hierarchy: ~/.claude/ → parent → project → subdirectory
Four permission modes balance control and convenience.
default: Prompts for first use of each tool
acceptEdits: Auto-accepts file edits for session
plan: Read-only analysis, no modifications
bypassPermissions: Skips all prompts (safe environment only)
Switch with Shift+Tab
Granular allow/deny/ask rules provide fine-grained control.
allow: ["Bash(npm run test:*)", "Bash(git:*)"]
deny: ["Read(./.env)", "Read(**/*.key)"]
ask: ["Bash(git push:*)", "Bash(rm:*)"]
Evaluation order: deny → allow → ask
Hooks let you run custom scripts before and after tool execution.
PreToolUse: Run validator before Bash commands
PostToolUse: Run scripts after tool execution
PermissionRequest: Custom permission logic
Can block, modify, or auto-approve based on custom logic
The "Lethal Trifecta" identifies three data theft risk elements.
1. Access to private data (env vars, credentials)
2. Exposure to untrusted content (web pages, user input)
3. External communication ability (network access)
"Text into your LLM = full control over what tools it runs"
Cursor is an AI assistant; Claude Code is an autonomous agent.
Paradigm: Cursor = Enhanced IDE, Claude Code = Autonomous Agent
Interface: Cursor = GUI (VS Code fork), Claude Code = CLI
Model: Cursor = User-selectable, Claude Code = Claude (optimized)
Execution: Cursor = User-initiated, Claude Code = Autonomous
Context: Cursor = IDE-provided, Claude Code = Full filesystem + shell
Think in files → use Cursor. Think in tasks → use Claude Code.
Cursor excels at: Quick inline edits, code explanation, GUI preference
Claude Code excels at: Multi-file refactoring, autonomous completion
Claude Code: Pipeline automation, tasks requiring shell access
Many developers use both for different contexts
OpenCode, Aider, and Gemini CLI offer different trade-offs.
OpenCode: 75+ providers, free — Budget, model flexibility
Aider: Code graph, git integration — Monorepos, explicit control
Gemini CLI: 1M context, free tier — Google Cloud, docs tasks
Codex CLI: GitHub Actions — CI/CD integration

Claude Code + Opus 4.5: 80.9%

Cline: 63%
Gemini 2.5 Pro: 63.8%

Ralph-Wiggum: iterative loops that treat failure as data.
"A while loop that feeds an AI agent a prompt until completion"
Deterministic stopping criteria (not "try once and fail")
Failure-as-data philosophy: setbacks guide refinement
Prompt-centric design: "LLMs are mirrors of operator skill"
The future is here—adoption is the primary challenge.
Old: Write code myself → New: Design workflows that write code
Old: One-shot prompts → New: Iterative loops until done
Old: Static instructions → New: Continuously improved artifacts
Old: Single session → New: Parallel agents on worktrees
Compound efficiency through workflow, context, and parallelization.
1. Claude Code = LLM + filesystem access = general agent
2. Workflows compound—every CLAUDE.md update improves the system
3. Context engineering is the fundamental skill
4. Parallelization via git worktree multiplies efficiency
5. The future is iterative loops that run until completion

Claude Code uses only four core tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash.
Read: File contents, images, PDFs
Write: Create new files
Edit: String replacement in files
Bash: Shell command execution
"Four tools outperform complex tool ecosystems" — Mario Zechner
MCP servers extend Claude Code with external tool capabilities.

/plugin install @anthropic-ai/mcp-server-context7
Available servers: GitHub, databases, APIs
Trade-off: Convenience vs. context window overhead

1 million token context window
60 requests/minute, 1000/day (free)
Deep Google Cloud integration
